sources.finding: Six Arch-family ISOs were downloaded and four of six source repositories pulled; Windows 11 and SteamOS were researched through documentation because no stable direct ISO URL was available.
sources.adoption: Treat Arch-family evidence as primary and Windows servicing evidence as conceptual input; never claim a Windows ISO or VM was tested.
sources.limitation: The corpus records downloads and clones only; it does not prove boot, install, or runtime behavior.

sources.finding: Windows 11 servicing uses CBS/SSU/WinSxS with transactional staging, sessions.log/CBS.log, pending operations, DISM ScanHealth/RestoreHealth and SFC; Arch-family systems use pacman, mkinitcpio, snapshots and bootloader-specific recovery.
sources.adoption: Map DISM/SFC read-only verification to pacman database/file checks, systemd unit verification, boot artifacts, lock ownership, snapshot readiness and reboot state.
sources.limitation: Research describes Windows mechanisms only; no Windows repair operation was executed or imported.

sources.finding: Cross-distro design decisions require observed state, snapshot-before-update, coupled boot artifacts, retained rollback state and a DISM/SFC-style reconcile-and-repair command.
sources.adoption: Keep the new rescue assessor read-only, fail closed on contradictory evidence, and leave mutation to the existing journaled repair path.
sources.limitation: The report is a design synthesis; it is not executable evidence by itself.

sources.finding: Captured DISM CheckHealth, ScanHealth, SFC verifyonly and reboot state can be classified without executing repairs; exact commands and narrow clean-output markers are required.
sources.adoption: Reuse the same fail-closed classifier shape for captured Arch-native probes with exact argv allowlists.
sources.limitation: Localized or unrecognized output remains unknown; the Windows module is not a native Arch replacement.

sources.finding: Windows servicing repair and journal reconciliation were analyzed as concepts; blind deletion of pending state is unsafe.
sources.adoption: Never let the Arch rescue assessor delete a lock or journal; require separate operator-approved recovery and fresh re-observation.
sources.limitation: No Windows VM or servicing mutation was performed.

sources.finding: An ownerless pacman lock is only a stale candidate and cannot authorize automatic deletion; unreadable process state fails closed.
sources.adoption: Port the lock-state vocabulary and repair_allowed=false rule into the engine assessor and stop automatic lock removal in the live repair command.
sources.limitation: The original module is a standalone pull artifact, not staged into the ISO image.

sources.finding: ALPM hook metadata can be validated structurally without executing hook commands; absolute Exec and known trigger/action fields are required.
sources.adoption: Keep native rescue evidence static or captured; do not execute hook bodies or inferred repair scripts.
sources.limitation: Metadata validation does not prove hook runtime behavior.

sources.finding: Suppressed mkinitcpio, dracut or kernel-install failures are unsafe unless nearby artifact validation exists.
sources.adoption: Treat kernel/initramfs/bootloader configuration as explicit observations and degrade when any are missing.
sources.limitation: The audit is a source review aid and does not regenerate boot artifacts.

sources.finding: Adopted patterns are traceable and must declare plan-before-mutation, journal-operation and verify-postcondition controls.
sources.adoption: Pin this research pull in a hash-verifiable catalog and require fail-closed evidence before any repair action.
sources.limitation: Catalog validation is provenance control, not a functional test of a target system.

sources.finding: The existing Windows assessor consumes exact read-only DISM/SFC evidence and reports missing, blocked, degraded and clean states without repairs.
sources.adoption: Preserve it as source evidence for the Windows-to-Arch mapping and mirror its status vocabulary in arch_rescue.py.
sources.limitation: It is Windows-specific and must not be executed from an Arch live environment.
